2.5.6.2 Criteria 2 - MCAL Kernel Execution Context
Secondly one needs to understand where the MCAL module kernel shall ideally reside/
located to limit the side effects of collisions on busses and bridges due to concurrent
access to HW peripherals from several cores. Defining a local kernel does not ex-
clude a multiplicity, to e.g. provide several kernels dealing with independent peripheral
modules or core individual resources. The following cases are defined:
• 2a: One Local kernel (executable on one core only)
• 2b: Global (distributed /shared) kernel (executable on any core)
